Operator: Good morning, and welcome to the Apex Energy Corp Second Quarter 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants will be in listen-only mode. After today's presentation, there will be an opportunity to ask questions. [Operator Instructions] Please note this event is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the conference over to Lisa Chen, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Lisa Chen: Thank you, Operator, and good morning, everyone. Welcome to Apex Energy Corp's Second Quarter 2024 earnings call. Joining me on the call today are Alex Rivera, Chief Executive Officer; John Ramirez, Chief Financial Officer; Tom Ellis, Chief Operating Officer; Mike Harlan, VP of Exploration; and Sarah Patel, VP of Marketing.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that some of the statements we make today may be forward-looking. These statements are based on current expectations and assumptions and are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a more detailed discussion of these risks.

I will now turn the call over to Alex Rivera.

Alex Rivera: Thank you, Lisa, and good morning, everyone. Apex Energy Corp delivered solid results in the second quarter, driven by strong operational performance and favorable commodity prices. We achieved robust reserve additions and production growth while staying under budget on key capital investments. I'm particularly pleased with our progress on exploration successes and cost efficiencies. We are focused on advancing our high-return development inventory across premier basins. Further, we are working on expanding our infrastructure footprint to support growing volumes. We continue to adjust to market dynamics through disciplined hedging and supply chain optimizations. Finally, we are taking steps to enhance shareholder returns while investing in long-term resource potential.

Now, I'll turn the call over to John Ramirez to discuss our financial results in more detail.

John Ramirez: Thank you, Alex. As Alex mentioned, we had a strong quarter. Our revenue was $2.4 billion, up 22% year-over-year. Operating income was $850 million, and net income was $520 million. We generated $650 million in free cash flow and returned $420 million to shareholders through dividends and share repurchases. Our balance sheet remains strong, with $4.2 billion in debt and $1.8 billion in cash.

Let me now turn to our capital expenditure performance for the first half of 2024, with a detailed breakdown across our key categories: Drilling, Completion, and Facilities. As you know, our H1 capex guidance was $1.2 billion, representing about 45% of our full-year $2.7 billion program, heavily weighted toward our high-margin Permian and Eagle Ford assets. We're pleased to report that we've deployed $1.15 billion through June—coming in 4% under budget—driven by operational efficiencies that have allowed us to accelerate activity without compromising safety or returns.

Let me walk you through the budget versus actuals, category by category, and provide some color on the drivers, trends, and forward outlook. For context, we've maintained our full-year rig count at 12 operated rigs—eight in the Permian, three in Eagle Ford, and one in the Bakken—while optimizing for longer laterals averaging 11,500 feet, up 15% year-over-year.

Drilling capex came in at budget $480 million versus actual $440 million, an 8% underrun. Drilling represented 40% of our H1 budget, focused on spudding 28 wells across our core acreage. We came in $40 million under plan, primarily due to enhanced drilling efficiencies from our adoption of advanced polycrystalline diamond compact bits and automated directional drilling systems, similar to those deployed by Pioneer Natural Resources in the Midland Basin. Our average days per 1,000 feet drilled improved to 1.8 days from 2.1 days last year—a 14% gain—saving roughly $2.5 million per well.

Regionally, in the Permian Delaware Basin, where 65% of our drilling dollars went, we benefited from pad drilling synergies on our 40,000-net-acre Waha position, reducing mobilization costs by 12%. Eagle Ford saw a slight overrun on two vertical pilots testing Wolfcamp C, but this was offset by Bakken efficiencies, where our wildcat in McKenzie County hit total depth in under 20 days. Overall, drilling cost per lateral foot fell to $450 from $520 budgeted, reflecting lower rig day rates amid softer service pricing—WTI holding steady around $82 per barrel has kept pressure on contractors.

Looking ahead, we expect Q3 drilling capex at $300 million, scaling to 15 spuds, with continued emphasis on our 2.5-year inventory of locations exceeding 50% IRR at $60 WTI.

Completion capex was budget $600 million versus actual $660 million, a 10% overrun. Completion, at 50% of the budget, was our largest bucket, tied to frac'ing 32 wells completed in H1. We overspent by $60 million here, driven by supply chain headwinds on proppant and sand—global logistics disruptions from Red Sea tensions increased railcar costs by 8%, echoing challenges seen across peers like EOG Resources. Additionally, we pulled forward some Q3 activity to capitalize on optimal frac timing around full moon cycles to minimize lost circulation risks in our Wolfcamp A/B plays.

That said, technical initiatives mitigated much of the upside: Our engineered completions using dissolvable diverter tech and optimized stage spacing—down to 180 feet from 220—boosted initial production rates by 18% to 1,800 Boe/d per well. We also trialed ConocoPhillips-style hybrid fracs with 40/70 mesh sand in Eagle Ford, achieving 10% higher estimated ultimate recoveries on early-time declines. Cost per frac stage rose modestly to $125,000 from $115,000 budgeted, but our drilling and completion capital efficiency improved 7% to $8.2 million per lateral foot.

Regionally, Permian completions absorbed 70% of spend, with Eagle Ford contributing strong returns from our Dewitt County pads. We're guiding H2 completions to $750 million, assuming sand pricing stabilizes post-Q3.

Facilities capex was budget $120 million versus actual $115 million, a 4% underrun. Facilities rounded out at 10% of budget, covering flowlines, separators, and water infrastructure. We underspent by $5 million, thanks to modular prefabrication strategies—partnering with firms like Chart Industries for skid-mounted cryogenic plants—which cut installation time by 25%. In the Permian, we commissioned two 20,000 bbl/d centralized facilities tied to our Pecos River assets, incorporating electric drives to slash Scope 1 emissions by 30% ahead of our 2025 net-zero drilling pledge.

Bakken saw efficient tie-ins to midstream via ONEOK laterals, avoiding $3 million in NGL takeaway constraints. Trends here are favorable: Facilities intensity dropped to $0.75 per Boe/d of capacity from $0.90 budgeted, aligning with ExxonMobil's low-cost models.

Net-net, our 4% H1 underrun positions us flexibly for the back half, with $1.55 billion remaining capex skewed 55/35/10 toward drilling and completion and facilities. We've clawed back $75 million in efficiencies through digital twins for drilling optimization and AI-driven frac design—early wins mirroring Occidental's playbook. Return metrics remain robust: Permian drilling and completion FCF yields over 60% at current strips, with NPV10 breakevens under $45 WTI.

We're maintaining FY24 capex at $2.7 billion, targeting 105,000 Boe/d exit rate—up 12% YoY—while preserving our $1.1 billion dividend and $500 million buyback capacity. Risks include service inflation if WTI dips below $75, but our hedge book at 65% protects through 2025.

Before I hand over to Tom for operations, let me touch on our operating expenses per BOE, a key metric underscoring our profitability amid inflation and supply chain issues. In Q2, company-wide OpEx per BOE was $9.45, an 8.5% improvement year-over-year from $10.33, and down 2.2% sequentially from Q1's $9.67. Trailing 12-month stands at $9.62 per BOE, placing us in the lower quartile among Permian peers like Pioneer and EOG, based on S&P Capital IQ benchmarking.

Historically, pre-COVID 2019 averaged $12.75 per BOE due to high service costs and legacy assets. The 2020 downturn drove it to $11.20 by year-end through pruning high-cost wells. Inflation peaked us at $10.85 in 2022, but we've reversed that with a five-year compound annual decline of 5.8%, outpacing the EIA upstream index up 15% since 2021.

LOE at 62% of total was $5.87 per BOE, down 10% YoY on run-time gains. Gathering and compression steady at $2.15, workovers up slightly to $1.43 from targeted Eagle Ford interventions. Visibility from SAP Ariba ERP.

Permian at $8.10 per BOE, down 12% YoY on scale—Delaware laterals with ESP lives to 850 days via monitoring. Eagle Ford $11.20 up 3% on water costs, Bakken $10.45 on logistics.

Our strategies: PetroAI platform on 85% of Permian wells cuts downtime 18%, drones 40% of inspections save 30% man-hours, upcoming ROVATI robotics. Supply chain: three-year Tenaris contracts 10% below spot, Halliburton chemicals down 14%. Water recycling at 72% in Permian saves $0.45 per BOE. Culled 45 high-cost wells, M&A synergies $0.60 per BOE. Hedged 40% diesel/power.

Q3 guide $9.20-$9.50 per BOE, potential $8.50 year-end. Risks labor, frac rates.

On capital allocation, our framework prioritizes sustainable dividends, opportunistic buybacks, and targeted reinvestment, backed by $12.4 billion YTD FCF up 18% at $82 WTI. Dividends top: $4.2 billion YTD, 4.3% yield, $0.92/share up 6%, 42nd hike, FY24 $18 billion at 1.8x coverage, stress-tested 1.3x at $60 oil.

Buybacks $3.8 billion YTD, 4.2% shares retired at $142 avg, 8% below 7.5x EV/EBITDA, EPS boost 12%, $6.2 billion left, $4-5 billion 2025 if attractive.

Reinvestment 45% FCF or $7.9 billion: upstream 65% $5.1 billion—Permian $2.8 billion 150 wells Super Wolfbone 2,800 boe/d, Guyana $1.2 billion Yellowtail, North Sea $800 million Buzzard. Mid/down 25% $2 billion—Corpus Christi LNG, Baton Rouge hydrocracker. Transition 10% $790 million CCUS Permian 5 mtpa.

Allocation: 40% returns, 45% growth, 15% balance sheet at 0.9x net debt/EBITDA. 25% TSR YTD.

Finally, our midstream segment delivers resilient fee-based cash flows. Throughput averaged 1.85 million Boe/d, up 12% YoY, 4% sequential. Crude 1.1 million bbl/d up 15% on Permian ramp, Waddell/EPIC at 92% utilization, Waha diff $0.75/bbl. Gas 4.2 Bcf/d up 8%, NGL 285,000 bbl/d up 10%; Appalachia MVP 95%, Mont Belvieu exports.

Tariffs $425 million up 18%, 85% take-or-pay, $0.85/bbl crude, $0.22/Dth gas, margins 62%. Permian 55%, Bakken 15%, Gulf Coast NGL up 22%.

Infrastructure $1.2 billion capex: Permian Connector 800,000 bbl/d online 75% contracted $120 million EBITDA; Marcus Hook NGL +25,000 bbl/d; Appalachia Connector 1.2 Bcf/d Q4 2025.

Electrification cuts methane 25%. EBITDA 14-16% growth to $1.75-$1.80 billion, volumes 2.0 MMBoe/d. Coverage 1.8x.

I will now turn the call over to Tom Ellis for an operational update.

Tom Ellis: Thank you, John. On the operational front, we continue to execute our strategy effectively. Our production averaged 92,000 barrels of oil equivalent per day. We successfully brought the Van Gogh pad online in the Permian Delaware, which is expected to contribute significantly to our production growth in the coming quarters. We are also making progress on our cost reduction initiatives through digital tools and water management.

Now I will turn it over to Mike Harlan for an update on our exploration activities.

Mike Harlan: Thank you, Tom. We are excited about the potential of our exploration program. We recently completed a successful seismic survey in the Permian Delaware Basin and are planning to drill 15 exploration wells in the next year. We believe these wells have the potential to add significant reserves to our portfolio, building on high success rates and advanced tech like AI geosteering.

Finally, I'll turn it over to Sarah Patel to discuss our marketing strategy.

Sarah Patel: Thank you, Mike. We are focused on optimizing our marketing strategy to maximize the value of our production. We are seeing strong demand for NGL products in the Gulf Coast market area, and we are working to expand our customer base and strengthen our relationships with existing customers. The impact of these efforts on our realized pricing is significant, supporting premium tariffs amid rising exports.

Operator, we are now ready to open the line for questions.

Operator: [Operator Instructions] Our first question comes from Sarah Jenkins with Energy Capital Partners. Please go ahead.

Sarah Jenkins: Thanks, and good morning team. I wanted to dive into your future development plans and resource potential. With WTI hovering around $75 and the macro uncertainty, can you walk us through the inventory runway, key projects, and how you're positioning for the next cycle?

Alex Rivera: Great question, Sarah, and thanks for joining the call. I'll take that one and hand over to our VP of Exploration, Mike Harlan, for the deep dive on the technical side. Overall, at Apex Energy, we're laser-focused on delivering long-term value through a disciplined, high-return development program anchored in our world-class asset base. We've got a decade-plus of low-cost inventory at sub-$40 breakevens, which positions us exceptionally well regardless of the commodity cycle.

Let me start with the big picture on resource potential. As of year-end 2024 projections, our proved developed producing reserves stand at 4.2 billion barrels of oil equivalent, or Bboe, with total proved reserves at 8.5 Bboe—up 12% year-over-year on the back of strong development drilling and revisions. When we layer in probable and possible reserves, our 2P book swells to 18 Bboe and 3P to 28 Bboe. Net resource additions last year were 1.4 Bboe, driven by a 96% success rate across 150 wells, and we're guiding for 1.2 to 1.5 Bboe in 2025. This gives us a reserves replacement ratio north of 150%, well above the peer average.

Turning to future development plans, our 2025 capital program is set at $5.8 to $6.2 billion, with 70% allocated to high-margin development drilling and completions, 20% to new exploration and appraisal, and the balance to infrastructure and tech pilots. We're targeting 15% production growth to 950,000 boe per day by year-end, with oil mix holding steady at 65%. Looking out to 2027, we see a path to 1.1 million boe/d, supported by a robust queue of 5,000+ locations across our core plays.

Mike Harlan: Thanks, Alex. Let's break it down regionally, starting with our flagship Permian Basin position—1.2 million net acres in the Delaware and Midland sub-basins, where we've delineated over 3 Bboe of 2P resources. Here, we're accelerating the Wyton Federal project, a 40-well pad in Lea County with lateral lengths pushing 15,000 feet. Early flow rates are exceeding 2,500 boe/d per well, with 30-day IPs averaging 1,800 boe/d—10% above type curve. Breakevens are sub-$35 WTI, and we're achieving half-cycle times under 9 months through our optimized frac designs incorporating 100-mesh sand and lower proppant intensity at 1,800 lbs/ft.

We're also layering in EOR pilots: two CO2 floods in the Central Basin Platform, mimicking Occidental's successful playbook, with initial response showing 15-20% uplift in recovery factors from the baseline 8-10%. Long-term, this could unlock another 500 MMboe in that acreage.

Shifting offshore to the Gulf of Mexico, our 25% working interest in the Olympus field—analogous to Chevron's Anchor—is a game-changer. First oil is on track for Q4 2026, with gross peak rates of 80,000 boe/d from subsea tiebacks to the Lobster host. We've certified 450 MMboe net 2P here, with high-pressure/high-temperature reservoirs yielding 25%+ net recovery via gas lift. Capex efficiency is impressive at under $25,000/boe, thanks to our alliance with TechnipFMC for standardized subsea trees.

Internationally, we're doubling down in Guyana, where our 20% non-op in the Yellowtail block mirrors ExxonMobil's Stabroek success. We've got 1.2 Bboe net unrisked resource potential from three appraisal sidetracks planned for 2025, with Liza Phase 3 FID imminent. In Namibia, our Orange Basin JV with Galp and Cosmo—similar to TotalEnergies' Venus find—spudded Venus-1X last quarter, hitting 150 feet of net oil pay in high-quality turbidites. We're budgeting $400 million for three more wildcats in 2025-26, targeting a 30% commercial success rate that could add 2 Bboe+ to our portfolio.

On the tech front, we're not standing still. We've rolled out AI-driven geosteering across 80% of our Permian rigs, partnering with SLB's DrillOps on cloud platform, shaving 20% off directional drilling costs and boosting footage by 15%. Electrification is key too: 50% of new pads will run on grid power by 2026, cutting Scope 1 emissions 30%. And we're advancing CCUS—our Permian hub targets 5 MMtpa CO2 injection by 2028, qualifying for 45Q credits and stacking with EOR for IRRs over 25% at $60 oil.

Alex Rivera: Spot on, Mike. Strategically, this all ladders up to our 'Fortress Assets' framework: focusing on Tier 1 inventory with >20% IRR at $55 WTI, while pruning marginal assets—we divested 50,000 acres of non-core Eagle Ford last quarter for $450 million to recycle into these drills. ESG is baked in; our methane intensity is down to 0.15%, beating API targets, and we're on track for net-zero Scope 1/2 by 2035 via offsets and blue hydrogen pilots.

In a world of OPEC+ cuts and LNG demand surging 40 MMtpa annually, our flexible portfolio—50% U.S. onshore, 30% deepwater, 20% frontier—de-risks us. We've got bolt-on M&A lined up, like the $1.2B DJ Basin tuck-in we closed in Q4, adding 300 locations at 4x cash flow. Bottom line: 10 years of drilling inventory at 10%+ returns, positioning Apex for 15-20% CAGR in free cash flow through the decade.

Sarah, does that cover it, or want more color on the Guyana economics?

Operator: Our next question comes from John Smith with Energy Capital Partners. Please go ahead.

John Smith: Good morning. Can you provide more detail on exploration and drilling activity updates, key well results, and future plans?

Alex Rivera: Thanks, John. Great to hear from you. Let me dive right into our exploration and drilling activity updates, as this remains the engine driving our multi-year growth profile here at Apex Energy Corp.

First, a quick snapshot of Q2 results: We spudded 28 wells across our core acreage, bringing our full-year D&C tally to 112 wells through the quarter—on track for our guided 450-475 gross operated wells for 2024. Our success rate held steady at 98%, with only one sidetrack due to minor lost circulation in the Wolfcamp C bench. Drilling costs continue to trend down sequentially, averaging $7.2 million per well in the Permian, a 4% improvement QoQ, thanks to our optimized pad drilling and PDC bit advancements from our partnership with Halliburton.

Let's break it down by region, starting with the Permian Basin, which accounted for 65% of our activity. In the Delaware Basin, our Northern Monument Draw asset delivered standout results from the seven-well Van Gogh pad. These 12,000-foot laterals in the Wolfcamp AXY interval posted average 30-day IPs of 1,450 boe/d—75% oil—with EURs north of 1.2 MMboe per well on an NPV10 basis of $14 million at $70 WTI. Proppant intensity was aggressive at 3,200 lbs/ft, with 45-stage fracs and tighter cluster spacing of 18 feet, yielding 25% better normalized IPs versus our 2023 vintage. We're seeing conductivity improvements from our diverter tech, which is reducing heel-toe variance by 15%. Inventory here remains robust at 1,800 locations, with 60% HBP.

Shifting east to the Midland Basin, our four-well pad in the Southern Waha area targeted the Spraberry/Dean stack. Initial rates averaged 1,100 boe/d, but early decline curves suggest we'll hit 900 Mboe EURs—solid, but we're iterating on fluid systems to combat the higher water cuts we're seeing amid the regional pressure depletion. Midland now represents 25% of our Permian mix, and we're layering in some secondary recovery pilots with CO2 injection, inspired by Occidental's successes.

Up in the Bakken, which is 15% of our program, we brought online five extended laterals from our Parshall field pads—averaging 14,500-foot laterals in the Middle Bakken. These wells flowed at 1,800 boe/d IPs (82% oil), outperforming our type curve by 12% due to our geo-engineered perf designs using machine learning from SLB's Delfi platform. Costs here are holding at $9.5 million per well, but with breakevens under $45/bbl, it's high-margin juice. We've got 450 locations queued up, and we're testing Nanotech tracers to refine our frac hits mitigation.

Internationally, exciting progress in Guyana offshore Block Z—our 20% carried interest JV with ExxonMobil and Hess. The Z-10 appraisal well, which we participated in spudding last month, confirmed a 400-foot oil column in high-quality Paleocene sands, with DST rates exceeding 8,000 bbls/d of 32-degree API gravity crude. This de-risks another 500 MMboe gross mean resource, pushing our net booking potential to 120 MMboe. FPSO hookups are on schedule for first oil in H2 2026, and we're budgeting $150 million capex this year across two exploration wells.

On the tech front, we're leaning into digital transformation: Our in-house seismic reprocessing with full waveform inversion has unlocked 200 drill-ready locations in the Permian that were previously muted. ESG-wise, we've cut freshwater usage 30% via produced water recycling, now at 85% substitution rates, and our electrification of two Permian rigs is shaving Scope 1 emissions by 20,000 tons CO2e annually—aligning with our net-zero 2050 pathway while boosting IRRs.

Looking ahead, Q3 D&C picks up to 120 wells, with seven rigs running steady in the Permian (up from six), three in Bakken, and one offshore support rig. Full-year capex is $2.1 billion, 55% to Permian, with $400 million earmarked for exploration. We're accelerating two Staggered Resource Plays in Delaware, targeting 15,000-foot laterals, and evaluating bolt-ons in the DJ Basin to diversify. At $75-80 WTI, our Permian inventory supports 10%+ annual growth through decade-end, with half-cycle returns over 100%.

Strategically, amid OPEC+ cuts and resilient global demand, we're prioritizing capital velocity—focusing on Tier 1 acreage where we control 70%+ working interest. No major M&A on the horizon, but we're in talks for midstream JVs to lock in low-fee takeaway, echoing EQT's model. Bottom line: Our drilling machine is firing on all cylinders, delivering peer-leading returns and positioning Apex for sustained FCF generation north of $1.5 billion in 2025.

John, happy to take a follow-up on any of this.

Operator: Our next question comes from Brian Lee with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

Brian Lee: Good morning. What are your expectations for capital allocation in the back half?

John Ramirez: Thanks, Brian. As I outlined earlier, we're sticking to our disciplined framework with strong coverage supporting continued returns.

Operator: Our next question comes from Emily Carter with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

Emily Carter: Could you please provide more color on cost management in operations?

Tom Ellis: Absolutely, Emily. Our initiatives around digital analytics and supply chain have driven the OpEx declines John detailed, and we'll keep pushing efficiencies.

Operator: Our next question comes from David Kim with Citigroup. Please go ahead.

David Kim: How will the results of the exploration program affect the company's future strategy?

Mike Harlan: Great point, David. The successes like Guyana and Permian delineate more Tier 1 inventory, reinforcing our focus on high-IRR projects as Alex and I discussed.

Operator: Our next question comes from Laura Wong with Barclays. Please go ahead.

Laura Wong: What is the outlook for NGL marketing in the coming years?

Sarah Patel: Thanks, Laura. Strong global demand and our expansions position NGLs for continued premium realizations, building on the midstream momentum John covered.

Operator: There are no further questions at this time. I would like to turn the conference back over to Alex Rivera for closing remarks.

Alex Rivera: Thank you, Operator. In summary, we are pleased with our performance in Q2 2024. We remain focused on executing our strategy and delivering value to our shareholders. Thank you for joining us today.

Operator: This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
